threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the bus is the best way to get around—everyone else knows it's the overground or a bike, especially with these tube strikes.
Last week on the N35, a guy serenaded the whole bus with old reggae tunes. Felt like I was in a mini concert at 2 AM, all of us swaying along.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I heard a saxophonist playing incredible jazz at 2 AM while waiting for the night bus on Karl-Marx-Straße. Pure Neukölln magic.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can overhear conversations about the best Döner spots while waiting for the U-Bahn at midnight. The city's late-night food culture is a unique blend of old and new.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local when they know the difference between a burrito from La Taqueria and one from Chipotle without a second thought.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy trying to teach his dog how to ride the bus at Civic Center. The pup wasn't having it, just plopped down in the aisle. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just Gaudí and art. They miss how locals actually prefer the no-frills bars where the wines flow and the gossip's even better.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a recent arrival by their struggle with the ‘Si, un café’ at local cafes; it's the stunned look when they realize it’s not just coffee.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You keep asking for a 'tube station' and the locals only direct you to the buses. You’ll soon learn, Dalston is all about that bus life.
Saw a group of kids on the 59 last night trading Polaroid photos like they were currency. Only in Brixton, right? Can't help but love this place.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a group of kids using an abandoned U-Bahn station as their skatepark. They were mixing creativity with graffiti, and it felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a late-night currywurst stand that also doubles as a small art gallery, showcasing local talents while you chow down.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local if they instinctively know to step over the Muni delays and still get to Dolores Park with a to-go burrito, no sweat.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 6 downtown yesterday—three people left a full cart of fresh lavender on the seat. The smell lingered long after they got off. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists assume all bars have free tapas with drinks—most locals don't expect them anymore. It’s a real treat when it happens!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still take a photo of the Sagrada Família every time they pass by, like it’s a brand new surprise.
